*Last updated: October 6, 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing.*


A due diligence questionnaire (DDQ) is a formal, structured set of questions an investor, buyer or procurement team sends to evaluate a company’s risks, controls and overall health before signing a deal or committing capital. DDQ software helps teams answer these questionnaires by retrieving approved knowledge, drafting responses with AI and routing them for review and sign-off.


This guide compares 8 response-side DDQ platforms, the tools vendors and fund managers use to answer questionnaires, by workflow, AI approach, knowledge management, pricing and reviews.


## **Best DDQ software at a glance**


Pick by workflow first, because tools built for SaaS security reviews, trust centers and investor diligence solve different jobs.


- **Inventive AI:** Best for source-backed answers that flag conflicting and missing information before submission.
- **Responsive:** Best for large teams that need business-unit separation and a trust center from one vendor.
- **Loopio:** Best for teams with a governed content library and standard ILPA and AIMA formats.
- **Arphie:** Best for teams that want structured review, with reviewer roles and question-level deadline tracking.
- **AutoRFP.ai:** Best for teams that prefer project-based pricing with unlimited users.
- **Conveyor:** Best for security teams that want a trust center alongside questionnaire automation.
- **DiligenceVault:** Best for asset managers and allocators that run diligence on both sides.
- **Ontra:** Best for private markets fund managers answering LP questionnaires.

## **How to evaluate DDQ software for your specific team**


Ask every vendor the questions below for your own team type before you compare features or pricing. The answers show which type of DDQ software fits your workflow.


### **For enterprise sales teams answering vendor DDQs mid-deal**


- **Unseen questions:** Ask each vendor to run a real DDQ that includes questions your library has never answered. A strong tool drafts a sourced answer from connected documents. A weak one leaves gaps or writes generic text your legal team rewrites.
- **Traceable sources:** Every answer should link to the policy, certification or past submission behind it, and reviewers should be able to open that document in one click.
- **Conflict detection:** If an older SOC 2 report says 99.9% uptime and a newer policy says 99.95%, the tool should flag the mismatch for a reviewer instead of picking one figure silently.


### **For security and compliance teams answering security questionnaires**


- **Trust center:** Ask whether it is included or an add-on, and what share of questions it can realistically deflect.
- **Questionnaire types:** Have vendors demo the formats you actually receive, such as SOC 2, ISO, SIG and CAIQ, rather than accepting a general claim of security questionnaire support.
- **Draft-to-approval speed:** Ask how many review rounds a typical answer needs, and whether you can see who owns an answer and where it is stuck.


### **For asset managers and fund operations teams answering LP questionnaires**


- **Industry templates:** Test the templates you receive, such as ILPA, AIMA and INREV. DiligenceVault and Ontra are built around investment-management workflows, while other platforms may need extra setup.
- **Consistency across cycles:** Ask vendors to demo a recurring LP questionnaire, not only a first-time response, to see whether prior submissions drive the draft.
- **Time to first draft:** Connected-source tools can produce a draft within hours, while library-first platforms need time to populate the library before they become useful.


## Best AI-Native DDQ Tools (Connected Knowledge)


These platforms read your existing documentation, sync with live sources, and draft answers without requiring a maintained library. Best for teams that want current information without content upkeep.


### 1. Inventive AI (best for source-backed DDQ answers with conflict detection)


[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) is an agentic AI platform built specifically for DDQ, RFP, and RFI responses, keeping humans in the loop for approval, aimed at sales, solution engineering, and presales teams.


#### How it works


Teams connect their existing sources (Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Salesforce), upload the DDQ and get a first draft in which every answer links to a source document. The platform reads the whole questionnaire before drafting, flags contradictions between sources and marks an answer as unavailable when no verified source exists. Reviewers then use assignments, bulk actions and approvals to finalize the file.


#### Who it fits


Enterprise sales teams answering vendor DDQs mid-deal within 24 hours, security and compliance teams handling security questionnaires in the same workflow, and small teams without a dedicated content manager.


#### Who it's not a fit for


- Teams that have a mature, well-maintained content library where reuse is already optimized.
- Teams that need predictable per-project costs instead of volume-based pricing.
- Highly regulated organizations that require all knowledge sources to be curated and approved before any AI touches them.


#### Inventive AI best features


- Whole-questionnaire reasoning: The agents read the entire DDQ before drafting, so answers stay consistent across sections.
- Connected knowledge: Syncs with SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion and Confluence, plus previous DDQs.
- AI Content Manager: Flags conflicting and outdated content across your sources before it reaches a response.
- Information unavailable flag: Marks a question as unavailable when no verified source exists, so reviewers see only answers backed by a real source.
- Collaboration and security: Role-based permissions, assignments and approvals, with SOC 2 Type II audited controls, SAML single sign-on and zero data retention agreements with its AI model providers.
- Verbatim mode: Keeps approved legal and compliance answers word for word.


#### Inventive AI limitations


- Reporting and analytics could be more robust for tracking DDQ performance, usage trends, and team efficiency.


#### Inventive AI pricing


Volume-based, tied to the DDQs, RFPs and questionnaires you process, with unlimited users and no per-seat fees. Plans start at $830/month billed annually. The[ROI calculator](https://www.inventive.ai/roi-calculator) estimates cost against your volume.

Arphie reads from Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Seismic, Highspot and URLs. Each draft carries its sources and a confidence level, so reviewers focus where judgment is needed. The platform imports Excel and Word, detects questions and sections and exports back to the same file format.

Enterprise teams with multiple document types, teams where reviewers must verify every answer before sending to buyers, and teams across Excel, Word and multiple knowledge sources who need structured approvals.


#### Who it's not a fit for

- Deadline tracking: Sets deadlines at the questionnaire, section and question level, with reminders by email, Slack or in-app.

## Best Library-First DDQ Tools (Maintained Content)


These platforms depend on a team member keeping a central library current. Best for teams with repeating questions, a named owner, and consistent workflows.


### 4. Loopio (for teams with a governed content library and standard ILPA and AIMA formats)


Loopio is best for teams with a governed content library that answer recurring formats such as ILPA and AIMA questionnaires. Loopio centers DDQ work on a structured Library, collaborative Projects and review cycles.


#### How it works


SmartScan identifies questions in incoming DDQs and recommends matching answers from the Library. The Governed Library organizes approved answers by category with owners and expiry dates. When the same question returns, Response Intelligence reuses approved wording verbatim. Audit trails report on answer history, approvals and content changes for compliance and legal review.


#### Who it fits


Teams with a named library owner, investment teams answering standard formats and teams with multi-language needs where consistency matters more than speed.


#### Who it's not a fit for


Small presales teams handling ad-hoc questionnaires without a dedicated library owner. Organizations needing conflict detection across source documents. Sales teams that need answers within 24 hours rather than weeks to populate a library.


#### Loopio best features


- SmartScan: Identifies questions in incoming DDQs and recommends matching answers from the Library.
- Governed Library: Organizes approved answers by category, such as security, governance, ESG and operations, with owners and expiry dates.
- Audit trail: Reports on answer history, approvals and content changes for compliance and legal review.
- Locked wording: Response Intelligence reuses approved wording verbatim when the same question returns.
- Global features: Supports business units and project translation across more than a dozen languages.


#### Loopio limitations


- Complex DDQ files can be difficult to import, particularly Excel spreadsheets with multiple columns and Word documents containing tables.
- AI-generated answers may still require significant review for technical or highly customized DDQ questions.
- Keeping the response library accurate can become difficult as outdated and duplicate content accumulates.
- Importing and exporting, particularly with PDFs, could be more flexible.
- Project uploads and document mapping may require more flexibility when identifying questions, sections, and subsections.

- Responsive’s AI relies heavily on a curated question-and-answer library, which means teams need to spend time maintaining and managing that library to keep responses useful and current.

## **How do you test and compare DDQ software before you buy?**


Run a proof of concept on a DDQ you’ve already submitted, then work out what each tool costs per completed DDQ. A demo shows ideal conditions, and your own questionnaire shows real ones.


### **How do you run a DDQ software proof of concept?**


- **Start with a known-good DDQ:** Pick one where you know the right answers, then score the draft question by question.
- **Ask a question outside your content:** A reliable tool marks it unavailable. A weaker one writes a confident answer with nothing behind it.
- **Plant a conflict:** Load an old and a current source that disagree, and check that the platform flags the contradiction.
- **Use your messiest file:** Import the multi-tab Excel workbook or portal form that slows your team down most, and confirm the structure survives export.
- **Measure reviewer effort:** Track review minutes per 100 questions and the share of drafts approved without a real edit. A fast first draft can hide slow review.
- **Audit security terms:** Confirm model-training terms, retention, encryption, data isolation and access controls before you sign. Our[security page](https://www.inventive.ai/security) shows how Inventive AI handles data.

### **How do you compare the real cost of DDQ software?**


The lowest starting price isn’t always the lowest total cost. Check these four things before you choose:


- **How volume is measured:** Platforms charge by seats, projects or questionnaire credits. Find out what happens when you go over your allowance.
- **Who needs access:** Seat-based pricing gets expensive once sales, security, compliance and subject-matter experts all need logins.
- **How much upkeep the content needs:** A library-first tool needs someone to keep it current, and that time never shows up in the software price.
- **What happens when information changes:** Tools that flag conflicts and show sources cut the manual review needed after the first draft.


To compare tools side by side, use this formula:


Annual software cost ÷ DDQs completed per year = software cost per DDQ


Then add the internal time your team spends maintaining libraries, searching for information, reviewing AI answers and chasing subject-matter experts. A tool with a higher subscription can cost less overall if it cuts manual work on every questionnaire.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best DDQ software in 2026?


Inventive AI is the best fit for teams that want AI-first response with connected sources, conflict detection and unlimited users at a fixed monthly cost.


### Who should own the DDQ response process?


One named owner should coordinate each DDQ, usually in sales operations, security, compliance or investor relations, depending on who sends and receives the questionnaire. Subject-matter experts in security, legal and finance supply and approve answers, and the owner tracks assignments and deadlines. DDQ software makes this easier by showing who owns each answer and where it is stuck.


### What is the difference between a vendor DDQ and an investor DDQ?


A vendor DDQ comes from a buyer and focuses on security, compliance, financial stability and operational practices. An investor DDQ comes from an LP or allocator and covers fund strategy, team, governance, risk and operations, often in ILPA or AIMA formats. The two need different knowledge sources and templates, so choose software built for the one you answer most.


### Is it safe to use AI for DDQ responses?


It is safe when the platform limits how your data is used and a human approves every answer. Before you buy, confirm model-training terms, data retention, encryption, data isolation and access controls. Inventive AI uses SOC 2 Type II audited controls, SAML single sign-on and zero data retention agreements with its AI model providers.


### Can DDQ software handle Excel, Word and portal-based questionnaires?


Most platforms import Excel and Word files, and some also handle PDFs and buyer portals. Support varies, especially for multi-tab workbooks and files with tables. Test your messiest real questionnaire during a pilot and check that the structure survives export in the requester's original format.


### What should you do when no approved answer exists for a DDQ question?


Route the question to the right subject-matter expert instead of letting the tool guess. A reliable DDQ platform marks the question as unavailable when no verified source exists, so reviewers see the gap. After the expert answers, add the approved response to your connected sources so the next DDQ draws on it.


### Can one tool handle DDQs, RFPs and RFIs?


Yes, Inventive AI handles all three. The workflow is similar, but depth differs, so test each format you actually receive. You can also read how to automate RFP and RFI responses. How do I measure DDQ software ROI? Multiply average hours per DDQ by monthly volume and your team's hourly cost, then measure the same numbers after 60 days. Track first-draft approval rate and time from upload to final review too. Most vendors offer an ROI calculator.
